newsitem.title: USA: NU net trimed by mild winter, Millstone.
newsitem.headline: NU net trimed by mild winter, Millstone.

text.p: Northeast Utilities reported a drop in first quarter profits saying the primary reason was the ongoing outages of the three nuclear power units at Millstone Station in Waterford, Conn.
The company said earnings were also hurt by a much milder winter, which was the primary reason first quarter retail power sales were down 3.7 percent from 1996's initial quarter.
Another negative was a $17 million net increase in the cost of amortizing regulatory assets, mostly as a result of a rate settlement approved last year by Connecticut regulators.
Somewhat offsetting was a continued drop in financing costs, Northeast said.
It said the Millstone outage resulted in fuel and purchased power expenses of $340.5 million in the first quarter, up from $311.7 million a year ago.
It said earnings dropped to $17.5 million, or $0.14 per share, in the latest quarter, from $65.5 million, or $0.51 per share, in 1996's first quarter.
